A1.justification: Both complete, readable 35-page PDFs describe GGBench. Corresponding text, tables, figures, mathematical content, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 15 models on GGBench, including results in Tables 4–5, performance breakdowns, error analysis, and human evaluation in Appendix B.6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original model evaluations, numerical results, error analyses, and human-validation outcomes.

M1.justification: The aligned text–GeoGebra-code–image construction pipeline, data-curation procedures, and generation workflows remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A. No method component is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,411 construction problems, eight geometric categories, three construction types, and three difficulty levels. No dataset, task, or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same five end-to-end UMMs and ten LLM/LRM systems participate in the comparisons in Tables 4–5. The newly cited CodePlot-CoT does not become an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain temperature 0.0, the same inference prompts, GPT-4o judge, scoring metrics, and human evaluation involving three experts and 100 samples per model. No experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: The category, construction-type, and difficulty analyses in Sections 4.4–4.6, four error types in Section 5, human-validation analysis, and three Appendix C examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Human-rating aggregation and Pearson correlation reporting remain unchanged. No repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: All reported scores and findings are retained. For example, Tables 4–5 give GPT-5 VLM-I 57.08, Human 83.06, and Pass@1 79.02 in both versions; Figure 19 retains Pearson r = 0.9295. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Scoring definitions and geometric reasoning in the construction examples are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, formal results, proofs, or derivations are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution, novelty claims, integrated understanding–generation evaluation objective, and claims about the gap between direct image generation and code-based construction.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning executable geometric grounding, the limitations of pixel-similarity metrics, and model failure mechanisms remain unchanged. No substantive applicability qualification or limitation is added.

D1.justification: The first-page Code, Website, and Dataset hyperlinks change their destinations from the opendatalab-raiser namespace to openraiser. This updates resource access instructions; implementation details and appendix prompts remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether resource availability improved.

R1.justification: v2 adds Duan et al.'s CodePlot-CoT as reference [11], supporting the introduction's existing statement about difficulties with complex geometric setups. All 77 earlier references are retained, without substantive changes to research positioning.

P1.justification: The displayed date changes from November 17, 2025 to January 15, 2026, and the arXiv stamp and citation numbering are updated. Scientific prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added reference causes limited bibliography reflow on pages 16–20, and citation numbers update within existing displays. All five tables and 22 figures retain their designs and placement, with no graphical additions or redesigns.

improvement.justification: The revision consists of one supporting citation, updated resource addresses and dates, and incidental bibliography reflow. Methods, empirical evidence, explanations, claims, and appendix documentation remain unchanged, leaving the paper's overall quality essentially the same.
